title: Detecting Dataset Bias in Medical AI: A Generalized and Modality-Agnostic Auditing Framework

bias_targets.methodology: Applying the G-AUDIT framework to quantify the utility (mutual information with task labels) and detectability (recoverability from input data using surrogate models) of patient race, ethnicity, and Fitzpatrick skin color attributes across EHR, ICU, and medical imaging datasets.
Using the G-AUDIT framework to measure the utility and detectability of patient sex as a potential predictive shortcut in skin lesion classification and stigmatizing language detection tasks.
Evaluating patient age as a potential dataset bias and shortcut in skin lesion classification through mutual information calculations and surrogate prediction models.
Assessing insurance types (e.g., Medicaid, Medicare, Private) as potential spurious correlations in ICU mortality prediction using G-AUDIT's utility and detectability metrics.

Quantifying the risk of models exploiting non-patient dataset attributes (e.g., image dimensions, acquisition year, clinical specialty, medical interventions, and missing data patterns) using the G-AUDIT framework to evaluate their utility and detectability within the data.
